items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Erroll Garner started on the downtown side of the street closest to Fifth Avenue. And I stuck my nose in and I thought, oh that’s cocktail piano and I came out again. And of course when I think I could have heard him probably the first night, I didn’t realize how marvelous he was. I did later on.

ctx.x: Did you make the scene at 52nd Street?

Oh did I? That was living. Because you’d go in one door and in another, and just on and on. You didn’t have to have cab fare. You just walked from one to another. And as I recall, I guess there must have been a minimum at the table, it was probably fifty cents or a dollar at most. But you could hang out at the bar. It was something else. I’ve never seen a photo with the signs out of the people I wanted to see all at once, but you know, occasionally you’ll see photos and it will be Don Byas and Stuff Smith and…

We had occasion to see a group in Los Angeles called the Statesmen of Jazz. I think they’re coming to New York pretty soon. It’s a nice idea that they’re trying to promote, that you have to be over 65 to be in the group.
